name: Least integer a(n) such that every graph on a(n) vertices has an induced regular subgraph of order n.
comment: a(6)>=28 and a(7)>=71. It is not known if the sequence is increasing.
link: Paul W. Dyson and Brendan D. McKay, Ramsey numbers for regular induced subgraphs, arXiv:2604.08215 [math.CO] (2026).
Paul Dyson and Brendan McKay, Ramsey Graphs (section Regular induced subgraphs)
S. Fajtlowicz, T. McColgan, T. Reid, and W. Staton, Ramsey numbers for induced regular subgraphs, Ars Combinatoria, 39 (1995) 149-154.
example: a(3)=6 because some graphs with 5 vertices (for example the 5-cycle) have no induced regular subgraph of order 3, but every graph with 6 vertices has one.
author: _Brendan McKay_, Mar 24 2026
